> I made some comments in a first look through but I will wait until things are cleaned up to go further.
> 
> Some general comments:
> 
> Init files need to be updated so that whatever needs to come out in the API reference documentation does so accordingly.
> 
> In terms of the xyz file coming out in the current directory, I am not sure if this is a default when the user is explicitly saving such as file - I assume there is value in the user having one of these. Or if its some byproduct during say plotting where I think it ought to be created by default in the users temp folder and arguably deleted once it has been consumed/used.
> 
> Perhaps the docs, via one of these classes or init file, should show a small example of an xyz file and some description should a user not have come across this before

I am not a chemist myself but apparently .xyz files are widely used among chemists. They all follow the same formatting. What I could do is add a link into the method's documentation in case someone doesn't know about them.

The file appearing in the working directory however is not a byproduct of anything and I believe should be changed. Any suggestions on how to handle file creation in qiskit?

> I am not a chemist myself but apparently .xyz files are widely used among chemists. They all follow the same formatting. What I could do is add a link into the method's documentation in case someone doesn't know about them.

If this is a standard 'xyz' file then I think the format I see here as an xyz example is non-conformant. I believe in this case the first line in the file should be the number of atoms in the file and the 2nd line is an optional comment to name the molecule. So the xyz data would start on the third line. And yes this format is used in chemistry.

> The file appearing in the working directory however is not a byproduct of anything and I believe should be changed. Any suggestions on how to handle file creation in qiskit?

If the file creation is always explicitly under the users control then noting its saved by default in the current directory if no path is provided in the method seems fine to me. I think my comment was in part due to seeing a comment in the code. If our code seeks to do this itself, which is what I meant by byproduct and I gave an example should it be needed for plotting, then that would be a different matter. For testing or anything else we would want to ensure these were generated in the temp directory - see Python tempfile - we have code in Nature already using this in places.

When trying to add ProteinFoldingResult to the API I ran into a problem. @woodsp-ibm maybe you can help me with it.
I have added ProteinFoldingResult to the init file in qiskit_nature.results . Now when we are trying to import ProteinFoldingResult we run into a circular import that we didn't have before.

- ProteinFoldingResult runs init  file from qiskit_nature.problems.sampling.protein_folding when importing Peptide.
- This file is importing ProteinFoldingProblem
- ProteinFoldingProblem is importing ProteinFoldingResult.
And this way we get a cyclic import. I believe that by avoiding that ProteinFoldingResult runs the whole init file and just importing Peptide it should work, but even if specify the whole path to Peptide it seems like I have the same problem.
Any idea on how to solve this?

This bug came from a typo in the name of a local variable inside of a function. 
I basically set:
``` python
side_aminoacids = self._protein_shape_gen._main_chain_aminoacid_list
```
Instead of:
``` python
side_aminoacids = self._protein_shape_gen._side_chain_aminoacid_list
```
There is a test for self._protein_shape_gen._side_chain_aminoacid_list, which is a part of the tests in ProteinShapeFileGen.

In regards of the depth shading the Axes 3DPlot has a parameter as to whether to do that or not.
>depthshade: 	Whether or not to shade the scatter markers to give the appearance of depth. Default is True.

Is this what the query was about "I am not sure I understand. The plot needs to be "3D" even if it doesn't rotate since it represents the shape of the protein. How would we turn that off?"

I guess I was wondering if it would be worth on the plotter we have to allow a user to change the value via that logic. We allow grids to be on or off, this could be another parameter that was passed on down. But then I guess we don't expose a way to change colors that its uses  either right, so maybe things are fine as they are and if the user wants/needs more they can plot it directly themselves.
